text:
sam: Customer hitting intermittent 401s during streaming. They see the stream start then after ~2-3s connection drops with 'Unauthorized'. They provided their client-side request id 01f3b7c2.
sam: Happening from their hosted account (api.redwood.ai). Their repro curl returns 200 when not streaming.
priya: thanks. can you paste the raw request headers and the exact curl they used? any proxy / corporate firewall?
sam: they sent this header blob: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED`, `User-Agent: MyApp/1.2.3`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Request-ID: 01f3b7c2`
priya: ok. first thing: ask them to reproduce with curl -v -N and capture stderr so we can see tls/http2 frames. also include an explicit x-rw-debug header so our side can attach the debug bundle.
priya: share this minimal curl to reproduce the stream (replace $KEY and payload):

```
curl -v -N 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01f3b7c2" 
  -H "X-RW-Debug: 1" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}],"stream":true}' 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" 2>curl-stream.log
```

priya: notes: `-N` disables output buffering so you see chunks immediately, `-v` prints headers/ssl/http2 info to stderr (redirected to curl-stream.log above).

sam: should we also suggest --http2? some customers have proxies that downgrade/terminate h2.
kyle: yes try `--http2` as well. also include `--no-keepalive` if their client or LB is reusing a socket incorrectly.
kyle: if the above reproduces the 401, ask them to share that `curl-stream.log` plus the `X-Request-ID` and timestamp window. we can then correlate in logs and pull the full debug bundle.
priya: if they can't reproduce with curl, ask for a small Node sample that mirrors their client. some libraries automatically retry or reauth mid-stream and that can cause a server 401. example node fetch snippet: 

```
// node 18+
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.KEY}` ,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Accept': 'text/event-stream',
    'X-Request-ID': '01f3b7c2',
    'X-RW-Debug': '1'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-chat-1',messages:[{role:'user',content:'hi'}],stream:true})
});
res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()));
```

jordan: infra-bot reports a deploy around the time customer saw the first error: `infra-bot: deploy/redwood-runtime v3.14.2 succeeded at 1755209800` — could be related.
priya: good catch. ask customer for exact wall clock time of the failure and we'll check pod-level auth refresh logs for that window.
sam: sent curl + curl-stream.log back to customer with the node snippet and asked for the wall time.
kyle: if we confirm it's server-side, tell them to include the header `X-RW-Debug: 1` in a follow-up request — that triggers us to persist a debug bundle tied to their `X-Request-ID`. we can then attach it to the case.
priya: final quick checklist to give customer: 1) run the curl above replacing $KEY, 2) capture stderr (`2>curl-stream.log`), 3) include `X-Request-ID` and `X-RW-Debug: 1`, 4) try `--http2` and `--no-keepalive`, 5) send logs + exact timestamps + region.
sam: thanks — I'll update the ticket and wait for their logs. :thumbsup:
